The Fourth Period reports that the veteran defenseman’s tenure on Long Island could be nearing its end, with Mayfield unable to crack the lineup on a consistent basis to begin the season. He has appeared in just two games and was not expected to dress Tuesday night against the Anaheim Ducks. Mayfield, who turned 34 last week, is in the fourth year of a seven-year, $24.5 million contract and holds a full no-trade clause this season, which drops to a 16-team no-trade list next year. He has not requested a trade to this point, but there is a growing belief that such an ask could come if the healthy scratches persist. Any move would require his sign-off, which may not be a tall order given his lack of playing time. Per the report, the Ducks, Kings, Blackhawks, and Kraken are among the teams looking to add on the back end, while Nashville and Toronto are also seeking help but targeting younger options. items.title: Report: Red Wings’ Dylan Larkin expands trade list to 10 teams
items.summary: Dylan Larkin has reportedly opened up his trade request to include more teams.
items.body: Dylan Larkin has reportedly opened up his trade request to include more teams. Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press reports that Larkin's trade list now includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. The now-former captain of the Red Wings requested a trade in the spring and St. James reported at the time that he was only open to a move to the Panthers, Wild and Golden Knights. While former general manager Steve Yzerman fielded calls for Larkin, once he was removed from his post on July 15, those talks stalled while the Red Wings searched for a new head of hockey operations. That search is ongoing but Shawn Horcoff was elevated to interim general manager in September and seemingly has the authority to complete a Larkin trade. St. James reports one of the reasons a trade has not happened yet is that the Red Wings continue to ask for "value-now" players instead of a package of prospects and draft picks. One team notably not on Larkin's trade list is the Montreal Canadiens, even after Canadiens fans chanted "we want Larkin!" during a recent visit by the Red Wings. Larkin has one goal and three points in six games for the Red Wings this season after missing training camp with an upper-body injury.

According to head coach Paul Maurice ( per Florida Hockey Now’s George Richards ), Markström is expected to miss the next 10 to 14 days after being injured in practice. Specifically, Markström’s injury is related to being struck by a puck in practice. Obviously, this is a reasonable risk for a netminder, though something clearly went wrong. The Panthers acquired Markström from the New Jersey Devils this past summer for his second stint with the club. He is in the first season of a two-year, $12MM ($6MM AAV) extension signed around this time last season. Unfortunately, the reunion hasn’t begun on a positive note. Markström’s performance has been fine, but the Panthers were likely hoping for a cleaner bill of health from their new starting netminder. Two injuries in the first month of the season aren’t ideal. When healthy, Markström has made six starts for Florida. He owns a 3-1-1 record in those starts with an .897 SV% and 2.21 GAA. He was playing for the MHL’s Krasnaya Armiya Moskva, scoring 14 goals and 41 points in 52 games with a +21 rating. Duda graduated to the KHL’s CSKA Moskva a year later, finishing with three assists in 14 games. After a one-year stint at Toronto Metropolitan University, Duda transitioned to professional life for the 2024-25 season. Since then, he has only played for the AHL Roadrunners, and that isn’t expected to change. Defenseman John Marino is dealing with an upper-body injury, though the Mammoth are expected to utilize their existing depth rather than have Duda make his NHL debut. Other than some injury concerns, the Russian blue liner has played relatively well in the AHL. Since turning pro, Duda has scored nine goals and 45 points in 103 games with a +28 rating, showing the two-way defenseman he could become in the NHL. Meanwhile, Carcone lands on the injured reserve as expected. The six-year veteran has not played since October 8th, and was given a week-to-week recovery timeline. Carcone is arguably coming off his best season, scoring 16 goals and 31 points in 79 games in the 2025-26 campaign. items.body: OTTAWA — Brady Tkachuk ’s finest moment as an Ottawa Senator may have doubled as his final great one with the club. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It has been a disappointing start to the year for the NHL’s three Californian teams. The Los Angeles Kings are the last winless team in the league, and both the Anaheim Ducks and San Jose Sharks sit at NHL .500 and comfortably back of the pace in the Pacific Division. While the Kings have an aging roster and are entrenched in a downward trend, both the Ducks and Sharks have young, talented cores and entered the year with high expectations. What are your concerns about these younger teams who were supposed to take the step forward in the Pacific Division? According to a team announcement , the Kings have activated winger Mats Zuccarello from the injured reserve. After the Philadelphia Flyers defeated the Ottawa Senators this past Saturday, the Los Angeles Kings remained the only team yet to win their first game of the 2026-27 season. First, Los Angeles has gotten dismal play from between the pipes, with the tandem of Darcy Kuemper and Anton Forsberg managing an .861 SV%. Hardly conducive to winning. Secondly, the Kings struggle to score, which has been a problem for a while. Last season, despite making the postseason for the fifth consecutive year, Los Angeles finished 29th in scoring. This season, albeit early, the Kings are 31st in scoring, just ahead of the Flyers. Fortunately, with Zuccarello returning, this should improve. He’s been limited to one assist in two games this season due to an undisclosed injury. However, even on the wrong side of 30, Zuccarello is one year removed from scoring 15 goals and 54 points in 59 games with the Minnesota Wild. It will take more than Zuccarello to turn things around, but there is a silver lining for the Kings. They have played the fewest games in the league so far, so there is still time to recover.

items.title: Can The Boston Bruins Shock The Rest Of The NHL's Atlantic Division?
items.summary: Through their first 10 percent of the 2026-27 campaign, the Boston Bruins s have been one of the NHL's most dangerous teams. But can their strong start last?
items.body: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Eric Canha-Imagn Images Can The Boston Bruins Shock The Rest Of The NHL's Atlantic Division? Adam Proteau Partner Oct 20, 2026 5:12 PM Published Oct 20, 2026 5:12 PM Through their first 10 percent of the 2026-27 campaign, the Boston Bruins s have been one of the NHL's most dangerous teams. But can their strong start last? After the Boston Bruins had a solid 2025-26 season, some observers – this one included – wondered whether they could replicate it, let alone improve on it. But in their first nine games, the Bruins have a 7-2-0 record, good enough for first place in the Atlantic Division and second place in the Eastern Conference. The good news doesn't stop there for Boston. They've won five straight games, and their plus-15 goal differential is the second-best in the entire NHL. Meanwhile, goalie Jeremy Swayman has a stellar .934 save percentage and 1.85 GAA, making him an early front-runner for the Vezina Trophy as the league's best netminder. More Videos Their overall depth has really shined as well, with a whopping 11 players who've generated at least five points. Boston's terrific start is another indication that the Atlantic is going to be one of the NHL's most competitive divisions, and Bruins fans have to be extremely pleased with head coach Marco Sturm, who is making a great case for the Jack Adams Award as the league's best bench boss. That said, it's still reasonable to be skeptical of the Bruins and where they rank among legitimate Stanley Cup threats. They are still very much a team transitioning from the Brad Marchand/Patrice Bergeron era, and have 12 players who are 27 or younger, and six players who are 30 years old or older. The Bruins of today are going to look significantly different than the Bruins team a year or two from now

items.summary: Roy suffered a lower-body injury earlier this month, leading to him being placed on injured reserve.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A veteran presence is set to return to action. The Washington Capitals have activated defenseman Matt Roy off injured reserve, with head coach Spencer Carbery announcing that he’ll be in the lineup on Tuesday night, when the Capitals play host to the Los Angeles Kings . Roy has missed the past six games due to a lower-body injury that he suffered back on Oct. 3 against the Tampa Bay Lightning . The Capitals have been solid during that time, going 4-2-0, winning each of their past two games, including a 4-2 victory over the New Jersey Devils this past Saturday. Roy was placed on injured reserve a little over a week later to make room for fellow blueliner Justin Holl. Roy’s injury came in the second game of the 2026-27 campaign. He was in the lineup for the season opener on Friday night, when Washington came away with a 5-2 win over the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes . Roy played 22:29 in the victory, but didn’t put his name on the scoresheet. The 31-year-old is in his third season in the U.S. capital. After five seasons with the Kings, the Detroit native signed with the Capitals as a free agent, inking a six-year, $34.5 million contract with the team in July 2024. After five consecutive seasons with at least 20 points , Roy’s production took a dip last season on a Washington team that struggled, posting just two goals and 19 points in 79 games. But teenagers like Gavin McKenna with the Toronto Maple Leafs, Alberts Smits with the New York Rangers and Ivar Stenberg with the San Jose Sharks are your future, and that's where handing out minutes becomes a balancing act for a coach. You're feeling the pressure to win now, especially in big markets like Toronto and New York. items.body: Brady Tkachuk isn't ready to let his Ottawa Senators jerseys go to waste. Tkachuk was granted a trade request to team up with brother Matthew in Florida over the off-season, spurning the Senators despite his captaincy. His first game back promises to bring some fireworks, with Tkachuk likely to hear raucous boos from the Senators faithful. "I think, once we get there, it’s going to hit a little more," Tkachuk said Monday. "Now it still feels like that game you circle on the calendar, and I bet for a lot of people, can’t believe it’s here, but once we land in Ottawa, set foot and see some of the guys, it’ll be, ‘All right, it’s here.' It’s going to be nervous, I’m going to be nervous. It’s going to be fun, a weird but cool experience, and yeah, I’m looking forward to it." Tkachuk totalled 213 goals and 250 assists for 463 points in 572 games with the Senators. He also guided them to back-to-back playoff appearances over the last two seasons. He missed the first three games of the Penguins’ season with an upper-body injury he suffered late in the preseason. If Rust is forced to miss a significant amount of time, Pittsburgh will have to find someone to take his place on Crosby’s right wing. items.body: Forward scores go-ahead goal against Sharks, wants 'to be a guy who is known for those big moments' TORONTO -- If Gavin McKenna has proven one thing so far in the infancy of his NHL career, it is that he does not shy away from big moments. In his first meeting against Ivar Stenberg , who was selected by the San Jose Sharks with the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NHL Draft, McKenna, the No. 1 pick by the Toronto Maple Leafs, delivered the go-ahead goal and eventually game-winner, the first of his career, in a 3-1 victory at Scotiabank Arena on Monday. “I think it’s just a confidence thing,” McKenna said. “For me, you want to be a guy who is known for those big moments, so when you get the time and opportunity to be out there on the ice, you want to make the most out of it. When you are playing with guys like Auston (Matthews), Willy (Nylander) and those guys, I think it just brings confidence in itself. So for me, it’s something I take a lot of passion in, is trying to be known as a guy able to perform in those situations.” McKenna's goal came during a power play at 4:56 of the third period. Matthews recovered a rebound behind the net and sent a short pass to McKenna, who took the puck on his backhand before spinning toward the slot and shooting under the glove of Sharks goalie Yaroslav Askarov to give the Maple Leafs a 2-1 lead. “Pretty fired up,” he said. “I think it’s a hard league to score in, so when you get to put one in the back of the net, it feels pretty good.” Instead of immediately shooting, the 18-year-old showed patience. He used the time he realized he had and pulled the puck back, allowing Nylander to skate in front of him toward the near side of the net, which added another threat for Askarov to consider, before taking an extra step and shooting to the far side.

items.title: Mammoth hold off late charge to beat Penguins
items.body: SALT LAKE CITY — Clayton Keller, Kevin Stenlund, Nate Schmidt and Nick Schmaltz all tallied a goal and an assist to help the Utah Mammoth beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 5-4 on Monday night. Kailer Yamamoto added a goal, and Sebastian Cossa had 15 stops for Utah. Erik Karlsson, Richard Rakell, Egor Chinakhov, and Declan Carlile each scored for Pittsburgh. Bryan Rust assisted on two goals. Arturs Silovs tallied 24 saves. Karlsson’s deflected power-play goal put the Penguins on the board just 71 seconds into the game. Keller levelled the score with a backhand at 6:00 of the first with his third goal in three games. Lawson Crouse snagged the puck near the boards and redirected it around Karlsson’s leg to Keller between the circles. Stenlund tapped in the puck from close range with 9:50 left in the first to give the Mammoth their first lead. Rakell tied it up on another power play goal at 7:01 of the second, flicking in a wrist shot near the left post. Utah surged back in front with a pair of goals late in the second. Schmidt reclaimed the lead with 8:16 to go, blasting a slapshot home from near the blue line. Yamamoto tipped in the puck from the low slot with 5:20 left to extend the lead. Schmaltz’s power play goal made it 5-2 for Utah at 1:36 of the third. Silovs denied his initial shot, but Schmaltz threaded a backhand around the goalie’s left leg on second effort. The Penguins cut the deficit to one late in the third period with goals from Chinakhov and Carlile. Chinakhov found the back of the net at 2:55 of the third. Carlile followed with a score off a wrist shot with 5:05 left.

items.body: NEW YORK — Sean Durzi scored 78 seconds in, Dylan Garand made 29 saves and the New York Rangers defeated the travel-weary Anaheim Ducks 5-2 on Monday night to improve to 6-0-0 at home this fall. The Rangers did not pick up their sixth victory at Madison Square Garden last season until Jan. 26, their 23rd game there. They lost 27 of 41 at home on the way to missing the playoffs and finishing last in the Eastern Conference. There is hope of a turnaround given this start, even missing franchise goaltender Igor Shesterkin for the rest of the season. Garand was making a fifth consecutive start since Shesterkin went down, and he has allowed two or fewer goals in nine of 10 NHL appearances dating to his debut last spring. He got support early and often, with Durzi's goal making it three home games in a row where the Rangers have a goal in the first two minutes. That has only happened once before for New York, in March 1989. Oliver Bjorkstrand scored twice, captain J.T. Miller and Gabe Perreault each had a goal and Alexis Lafrenière recorded two assists. Pavel Dorofeyev, the team's most notable trade acquisition over the summer, came close on several occasions but remained stuck on two goals for the season. Putting goalie Ville Husso in a tough spot with sloppy play, the Ducks looked every bit like a group that endured a 15-hour, delay-filled travel ordeal to the East Coast from southern California. They did not arrive at their hotel until 2:30 a.m., were on the ice for their morning skate less than nine hours later and were getting shut out until scoring twice in the final 70 seconds. Higgins, 45, appeared in court on Monday and rejected a plea agreement. Johnny Gaudreau, who played 11 seasons in the NHL with the Calgary Flames and Columbus Blue Jackets , and his brother Matthew Gaudreau died on Aug. 29, 2024, after they were struck by a car while riding their bikes near their family's home in rural New Jersey. items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Cole Knuble has fond memories of the Philadelphia Flyers ' home arena from his father, Mike, playing for them during his lengthy career. On Monday night, he made his NHL debut for the team he grew up rooting for, with his parents in attendance. The 22-year-old was one of three players called up from Lehigh Valley of the American Hockey League to fill in for injured forwards Owen Tippett, Tyson Foerster and Travis Konecny against Colorado. “Obviously I have been a fan of this team my whole life, so I think it’s extra special,” Knuble said. A fourth-round pick in the 2023 draft, Knuble nearly made the team out of training camp. He was disappointed to get sent to the minors but quickly adjusted his thinking. “I came (to camp) trying to make the team,” Knuble said. “But I think once I got down to Lehigh, the staff was so great. Most notably, the first-year NHL coach said, "To my knowledge, no," when asked if there was any concern Demko might not play in the 2026-27 season. "It's a slow process for him, but he is getting better," said Malhotra about Demko's recovery from hip surgery in January 2026. items.summary: The Buffalo Sabres may have their captain back sooner rather than later.
items.body: The Buffalo Sabres may have their captain back sooner rather than later. Rasmus Dahlin told reporters on Monday that he's "ready" to return after missing the team's last three games with an upper-body injury. The Sabres defenceman took part in practice on Monday for the first time since Oct. 11 and is expected to suit up against the Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday. “I think I’ll be ready. We’ll see here tomorrow and go from there,” Dahlin said. His injury occurred last week in a win against the Florida Panthers, when he left early in the second period while reaching for his back after putting a shot on goal. Dahlin exited after 7:08 of ice time in the first period, chipping in a goal as part of the 5-3 victory. Speaking to reporters on Monday, the Norris Trophy finalist from a year ago made it clear he wasn't all too concerned with the injury. “I knew it wasn’t going to be long, let’s just say that. I didn’t think it was going to take a full week.” “He had a couple good days while we were gone,” Sabres coach Lindy Ruff added. “Got him back in practice and see how he handles that today. But I thought he looked good.” Dahlin has two goals and two assists through six games this season. Once back on the ice, the 26-year-old will try to replicate his stellar production from a year ago, when he racked up a career-high 74 points (19 goals, 55 assists) in 77 regular-season appearances. He then added another four goals and 10 helpers in 13 games during the Sabres playoff run — the franchise's first post-season berth since 2011.

items.summary: The Ottawa Senators rewarded head coach Travis Green with a multi-year extension on Monday. The new contract provides Green with the opportunity to lead the Senators into contention, Adam Stanley writes.
items.body: OTTAWA – With a laugh, Travis Green said there are times as a head coach in the NHL where you’re forced to get a lot of takeout because going out for dinner would mean staring an angry fan base in the face. items.title: How EBUGs help with NHL goalie load management
items.summary: Some NHL teams are using their emergency backup goalies in practice and bringing them on the road.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis The NHL is requiring each team to have a full-time emergency backup goalie on its roster, under the new collective bargaining agreement. Some teams are going one step further. NHL.com correspondent Kevin Woodley wrote a piece last week on how EBUGs can help full-time netminders with load management throughout the season. Several NHL teams have their EBUGs travel with them on the road, and others used theirs to take the majority of shots in practice. On a special Monday roundtable episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Woodley joins former NHL goaltenders Carter Hutton and Devan Dubnyk to discuss EBUGs and how the role has evolved in the last few years. Carter Hutton : What did you find out as you started to peel back the layers of this new EBUG situation in the NHL? Kevin Woodley : Even on a gameday skate, goalies are basically out there as a target. Think of a daily practice: if you’re facing 20 rush drills, you can’t go hard on all 20. You might take five good reps then you have to back off. At some point, it’s diminishing returns and you’re not doing yourself any good. You’re just out there as target practice. Some of the guys I talked to for the article, they hoped that EBUGs could be a big difference for goalie injuries. Jake Oettinger of the Dallas Stars said a lot of his practices were just to make sure guys had a target, an NHL-quality target, not a zamboni driver. items.summary: Duehr has yet to play this season due to a lower-body injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Terrence Lee-Imagn Images A veteran forward is now up for grabs in the NHL. On Monday, the Winnipeg Jets placed winger Walker Duehr on waivers, making him eligible to be claimed by any of the other 31 NHL teams. If Duehr clears waivers, the Jets can assign him to their American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Manitoba Moose. The Sioux Falls, South Dakota native has yet to play this season due to a lower-body injury he sustained during Winnipeg’s preseason. He was medically cleared and able to fully join Jets practice on Friday, and is now being waived with the intent of sending him to the AHL. Duehr, 28, went scoreless in three games for Winnipeg last season. In 62 games for Manitoba, he notched 17 goals and 17 assists for 34 points, before contributing a goal and two assists for three points in the team’s seven playoff games. After a four-year collegiate career with Minnesota State University, Mankato, Duehr signed with the Calgary Flames as an undrafted free agent in April of 2021. In three-plus seasons with the Flames’ organization, he played a total of 84 NHL games while totaling nine goals and 10 assists for 19 points. In January of 2025, Duehr was waived by Calgary and claimed by the San Jose Sharks . In eight games for San Jose over the remainder of the 2024-25 season, he had two goals and no assists. Ahead of the 2025-26 season, Duehr signed a one-year, two-way contract with the Jets. This past offseason, he signed a two-year, $1.75 million deal to stay with Winnipeg. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Goaltending in the NHL is a tough gig. You’ve got to stop a piece of vulcanized rubber coming at you speeds of 60 to 90 miles per hour about 30 times per game, and if you don’t do so often enough, you’ll get the lion’s share of blame for your team’s struggles. items.summary: Canada has a lot of new faces on the roster, as they seek redemption when they head to Denmark next month.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The crew set to don the maple leaf next month has been set. On Monday, Hockey Canada released the 25-player roster set to compete in the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship in Denmark next month. It’s going to be a very different-looking Canadian roster in action, as new general manager Daniele Sauvageau has made some tweaks to fill some holes. Marie-Philip Poulin will not be playing this year, as she’s recovering after undergoing knee surgery over the summer. Also, national team regulars Sarah Nurse, Jocelyne Larocque, Emerance Maschmeyer Natalie Spooner, Claire Thompson and Blayre Turnbull are also not on the roster. Thompson retired from hockey after last season, while Turnbull is stepping away from the game, as she’s set to become a mother in the near future. Some returners from past national team rosters are looking to shine once again. With Poulin gone, Sarah Fillier will be asked to take an even greater role in leading Canada’s offensive attack. She’ll be flanked by Daryl Watts, who led Canada in scoring at last February’s Winter Olympics. As expected, Ann-Renee Desbiens, who has been Canada’s No. 1 since the 2021 Women’s Worlds, is expected to lead the team throughout the tournament, with youngsters Kayle Osborne and Eve Gascon behind her. While other veterans such as Laura Stacey, Erin Ambrose and Renata Fast remain, there will be plenty of first-time participants at the Women’s Worlds. Caitlin Kraemer, Rebecca Leslie, Sara Manness, Hayley McDonald, Rosalie Tremblay and Sarah Wozniewicz look to be impact players. items.body: The Winnipeg Jets - Connor Hellebuyck standoff is nearing a flashpoint. Hellebuyck, who did not attend training camp amid a trade request, will have his unpaid suspension end Friday, two days before the Jets host the Montreal Canadiens in the Heritage Classic. If the Vezina Trophy-winning goalie isn't dealt by then, however, then things could get sticky. That's what I expect to happen," Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Monday's episode of 32 Thoughts: The Podcast . The Jets have held out on trading the former league MVP Hellebuyck since he asked for a move in the wake of last season's playoff miss. To that end, per Friedman, three teams hold the keys to a Hellebuyck move. The Buffalo Sabres have long been reported as a team that has mutual interest with Hellebuyck. items.title: ‘I’m going to be nervous’: Panthers’ Brady Tkachuk on Ottawa return
items.body: Wednesday promises to be an emotional game for Brady Tkachuk . The Florida Panthers forward will return to Ottawa for the first time since being traded to take on the Senators. Tkachuk spent the first eight years of his career with the Senators and the final five as captain. He was traded early in the off-season to the Panthers after he requested a trade. "I think, once we get there, it’s going to hit a little more," Tkachuk said. "Now it still feels like that game you circle on the calendar, and I bet for a lot of people, can’t believe it’s here, but once we land in Ottawa, set foot and see some of the guys, it’ll be, ‘All right, it’s here.' It’s going to be nervous, I’m going to be nervous. It’s going to be fun, a weird but cool experience, and yeah, I’m looking forward to it." Tkachuk totalled 213 goals and 250 assists for 463 points in 572 games with the Senators. He also guided them to back-to-back playoff appearances over the last two seasons. His relationship with the franchise appeared to crumble after he represented the U.S. at the 2026 Winter Olympics and defeated Canada in the gold-medal game. Even with the bitter ending, Tkachuk knows it will be difficult to return to where he called home for so long. "Honestly, I haven’t thought of it too much, so I think once we get there, I think for me is kinda using that emotion to my advantage because it is going to be emotional individually and, in the building, so just be able to channel that and use that in the right areas because it’s going to be special for me to be back there," Tkachuk said. items.body: Players take morning skate before game against Rangers despite cross-country trip lasting 15 hours NEW YORK -- The Anaheim Ducks' four-game road trip to the East Coast got off to a turbulent start Sunday with a cross-country journey they won't soon forget. Their voyage from Southern California to New York took 15 hours with a three-hour time difference tossed into the mix. It included having to change airports -- and airplanes -- because of rerouting and mechanical issues. The travel day started at 8:30 a.m. PT. The players, coaches and traveling staff either took a team bus or drove themselves to John Wayne Airport in Santa Ana, California, to be on time for a scheduled 9:30 a.m. departure. The problem, however, was the team plane never got there. It had to be re-routed to Los Angeles International Airport, known to travelers as LAX. So, the Ducks boarded a bus at John Wayne Airport and left at 10:30 a.m. PT to drive to LAX. "We watched football, snapped cards around a bit," defenseman Jackson LaCombe said. "Honestly, just good with it the whole time. It was good camaraderie hanging with the guys." LaCombe said the players were watching NFL RedZone the entire time. In fact, he said they were talking on the plane about how fortunate they were that this was happening to them on a Sunday so they could at least watch NFL games. items.body: Rising stars more focused on getting Maple Leafs, Sharks untracked than personal battle TORONTO -- Gavin McKenna wants to make one thing clear about how he views his first game against Ivar Stenberg . "Obviously, a lot of talk between us and he is a good player," McKenna said. The Maple Leafs (3-4-2) have lost three straight (0-2-1) while the Sharks (4-3-1) have lost three of their past four (1-2-1). "We're hungry," McKenna said. items.body: The Ottawa Senators will be without their captain for the foreseeable future. Newly extended head coach Travis Green told reporters on Monday that the forward was "going to be out, probably ... a week to two weeks," with an upper-body injury. Chabot left Saturday's 3-1 loss to the Philadelphia Flyers with the injury and was seen shaking his hand in the penalty box during the first period before exiting. He was a minus-1 with one shot on goal in 12:03 of ice time through the first two periods. While it's unclear when exactly the injury occurred, Green did reveal that Chabot had been playing banged-up before Saturday. "He played a game with (the injury) ... it might have been the game before the last one," Green said. "It happened early, finished the game, and then he thought he would be fine, but couldn't go." Chabot was named the 11th captain in Senators history ahead of the season (and became the first francophone to wear the "C" in Ottawa), replacing Brady Tkachuk, who was traded to the Florida Panthers. items.title: Brady Tkachuk, McDavid, Kaprizov named NHL’s three stars of the week
items.body: The Florida Panthers forward was named the NHL's first star of the week after a goal-filled seven days of action, the league announced on Monday. Tkachuk became the third player in league history and the first in 40 years to record back-to-back natural hat tricks. He finished the week with six goals and four assists for 10 points in four games. Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid and Minnesota Wild star Kirill Kaprizov were named the second and third stars, respectively. McDavid has been on a scoring tear to begin the season, leading the league with 23 points through eight games. He totalled 10 points over the past week with three goals and seven assists in three games. The 29-year-old finished his week with an electric five-point performance in the Oilers' 6-2 win over the Utah Mammoth on Saturday. Kaprizov, meanwhile, became the first player in the NHL to hit 10 goals this season when he lit the lamp in Sunday's win over the Columbus Blue Jackets. The Russian had four goals and three assists for seven points over the last week.

items.summary: Swayman has the Bruins on a hot start in the opening weeks of the 2026-27 season, and is looking like one of the best in the NHL.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Griffin Hooper-Imagn Images One of the hottest teams in the NHL in the early weeks of the 2026-27 season is the Boston Bruins, with a lot of thanks going to their netminder. After a bumpy 2024-25 season following an elongated contract dispute, Bruins goaltender Jeremy Swayman has shown why he earned an eight-year contract, especially this year. The 27-year-old has helped Boston reestablish itself as one of the top teams in the Atlantic Division, with the team currently fighting for the top spot in the Eastern Conference. While there’s a lot of hockey to be played in the expanded 84-game regular season, Swayman has been a key part of the B’s exceptional start to the young campaign. In seven games, Swayman has a record of 6-1-0, tied with former teammate and Ottawa Senators star Linus Ullmark, as well as the Minnesota Wild’s Jesper Wallstedt, for the most wins so far in the NHL. Swayman also has a 1.85 goals-against average, a .934 save percentage and one shutout. If he can find some consistency and keep those numbers the same for most of the season, we might see Swayman in the Vezina Trophy conversation. Even in a league with so many talented netminders, Swayman has the ability to be a gamechanger for the Bruins, something that can put him in line for an award. On Monday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , former NHL netminder Devan Dubnyk explains why Swayman deserves to be in the Vezina Trophy. Devan Dubnyk: I think that Boston is looking pretty damn good, and he’s kind of been, I mean, he’s always been great. He’s obviously had his one down year, but I think this year he just looks as good as he has. When he’s going, he’s lights out. I think Boston’s got a good squad too.
